title: Parking lot
scopeHtml: Scope: requirements, entities, class diagram, Strategy and Facade, runnable Java and Kotlin, CAS-based thread-safe version, follow-ups. Questions are still to be written.

notes.title: Requirements
notes.html:
Design a parking lot: cars enter, get a ticket and a spot, and pay when leaving. In an LLD interview you first pin down what is in and out of scope, then say it out loud.

Functional (what we build):

  • Several spot sizes (bike, car, truck). A vehicle can use a spot of its size or bigger (a bike may use a car spot only if no bike spot is free).
  • park(plate, type) returns a ticket with the spot, or "full" for that size.
  • unpark(ticket) frees the spot and returns the fee. Fee is per started hour, with a rate per vehicle type.

Non-functional: pricing and spot choice must be swappable (open/closed), and two cars must never get the same spot.

Out of scope for the first 30 minutes: multiple floors, payment gateways, EV charging, reservations. Mention them in Follow-ups.

Worked example. 4 spots (1 bike, 2 car, 1 truck). A car enters at t=0 and leaves after 2 h 1 min. Started hours = ceil(2.0167) = 3. Car rate 30 per hour, so the fee is 90.

Industry examples. Airport and mall systems (Skidata, Flowbird) work exactly like this: a ticket, an entry sensor and a rate table; Indian FASTag lots skip the ticket and key on the plate.

Everyday analogy. A cloakroom: you hand something in, get a numbered token, and the attendant must never give two people the same hook.

Common interview traps.

  • Starting to code before asking about sizes, floors and pricing.
  • Forgetting the "full" case: park must be able to say no.

notes.title: Core entities
notes.html:
Nouns in the requirements become classes:

  • Spot: id, the biggest vehicle it fits, and a taken flag.
  • Ticket: id, the spot, the plate, entry time. It is the proof of parking.
  • VehicleType: an enum ordered by size, so fits is just ordinal comparison.
  • ParkingLot: the facade. It holds spots and active tickets and exposes park and unpark.
  • SpotStrategy and PricingStrategy: the two parts that change, so they are interfaces.

Why the ticket holds the spot and not just an id. unpark becomes O(1): no search over all spots. This is the data-structure choice interviewers watch for.

Decision gravity. Splitting strategies out is cheap to do now and reversible; hard-coding fee math inside ParkingLot makes "add weekend pricing" a risky edit later. Using an enum for sizes is a mild one-way door: adding "EV" or "handicapped" spots later means a second dimension (spot attributes), not a new enum value.

Everyday analogy. The ticket is the cloakroom token; the strategies are the attendant's rulebook and the price list pinned on the wall.

Common interview traps.

  • Making Vehicle a class hierarchy (Car, Bike, Truck) when only the size matters. An enum is enough until behaviour differs.
  • Searching all spots to find the car on exit.

notes.title: Class diagram
notes.html:
+--------------------+        +------------------+
 | ParkingLot         |------->| SpotStrategy     |<|-- NearestFreeSpot
 |  spots: List<Spot> |        | pick(spots, v)   |
 |  active: Map<id,T> |        +------------------+
 |  park(plate, v)    |        +------------------+
 |  unpark(id, now)   |------->| PricingStrategy  |<|-- HourlyPricing
 +--------------------+        | fee(v, duration) |
        | has many             +------------------+
        v
 +--------------+    1   issued for   1  +----------------+
 | Spot         |<-----------------------| Ticket         |
 |  id, type    |                        |  id, spot,     |
 |  taken(atomic)|                       |  plate, entry  |
 +--------------+                        +----------------+
 enum VehicleType { BIKE, CAR, TRUCK }   (ordered by size)

Read it as: ParkingLot owns spots and tickets, and delegates two decisions (which spot, how much) to strategies. A subclass SafeParkingLot (Concurrency section) changes only how state is protected.

Common interview traps.

  • Drawing arrows without saying what they mean (owns, uses, inherits).
  • Putting fee() on Ticket: then pricing cannot vary without touching the ticket.

notes.title: Key patterns
notes.html:
• Strategy (SpotStrategy, PricingStrategy). Why: spot choice (nearest, tightest fit, near the lift) and pricing (hourly, daily cap, weekend) change independently of the lot. Alternative: if/else on a mode flag, which breaks open/closed. Reversible and cheap.
  • Facade (ParkingLot). Callers see two methods, not spots and tickets. Alternative: expose the lists, which leaks internals.
  • Factory (optional). A ParkingLotFactory.build(config) that creates spots from a floor plan. Skip it unless asked; naming it is enough.
  • Singleton? Avoid. Many answers make the lot a Singleton. That hurts tests (shared state) and multi-lot support. Pass it in by constructor instead.

Industry examples. Spring's PlatformTransactionManager and Java's Comparator are Strategy in the wild; Android's RecyclerView.LayoutManager is a Strategy chosen by the app.

Everyday analogy. A taxi meter: the meter (lot) stays the same, the tariff card (strategy) changes by city.

Common interview traps.

  • Naming patterns without tying each to a real change you expect.
  • Using Singleton and then being unable to unit test.

notes.title: Code
notes.html:
Java (compiled and run with JDK 21). It is a single file: copy it into Demo.java together with the Run and test section.

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.*;

enum VehicleType { BIKE, CAR, TRUCK }

class Spot {
    final int id;
    final VehicleType type;           // the biggest vehicle this spot fits
    final AtomicBoolean taken = new AtomicBoolean(false);
    Spot(int id, VehicleType type) { this.id = id; this.type = type; }
    boolean fits(VehicleType v) { return v.ordinal() <= type.ordinal(); }
}

class Ticket {
    final String id; final Spot spot; final String plate; final long entryMs;
    Ticket(String id, Spot spot, String plate, long entryMs) {
        this.id = id; this.spot = spot; this.plate = plate; this.entryMs = entryMs;
    }
}

interface SpotStrategy { Optional<Spot> pick(List<Spot> spots, VehicleType v); }

class NearestFreeSpot implements SpotStrategy {           // spots are sorted by distance to the gate
    public Optional<Spot> pick(List<Spot> spots, VehicleType v) {
        Spot best = null;
        for (Spot s : spots)
            if (!s.taken.get() && s.fits(v) && (best == null || s.type.ordinal() < best.type.ordinal()))
                best = s;                                  // tightest fit wins, first by distance on ties
        return Optional.ofNullable(best);
    }
}

interface PricingStrategy { long fee(VehicleType v, long durationMs); }

class HourlyPricing implements PricingStrategy {
    private final Map<VehicleType, Long> perHour = Map.of(
        VehicleType.BIKE, 10L, VehicleType.CAR, 30L, VehicleType.TRUCK, 80L);
    public long fee(VehicleType v, long ms) {
        long hours = Math.max(1, (ms + 3_599_999) / 3_600_000);   // ceil, minimum 1 hour
        return hours * perHour.get(v);
    }
}

class ParkingLot {
    protected final List<Spot> spots;
    protected final SpotStrategy strategy;
    protected final PricingStrategy pricing;
    protected final Map<String, Ticket> active = new HashMap<>();
    protected final Map<String, VehicleType> kind = new HashMap<>();
    protected int seq = 0;

    ParkingLot(List<Spot> spots, SpotStrategy s, PricingStrategy p) {
        this.spots = spots; this.strategy = s; this.pricing = p;
    }

    Optional<Ticket> park(String plate, VehicleType v, long nowMs) {
        Optional<Spot> pick = strategy.pick(spots, v);
        if (pick.isEmpty()) return Optional.empty();           // lot full for this size
        Spot s = pick.get();
        s.taken.set(true);
        Ticket t = new Ticket("T" + (++seq), s, plate, nowMs);
        active.put(t.id, t); kind.put(t.id, v);
        return Optional.of(t);
    }

    long unpark(String ticketId, long nowMs) {
        Ticket t = active.remove(ticketId);
        if (t == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("unknown ticket " + ticketId);
        t.spot.taken.set(false);
        return pricing.fee(kind.remove(ticketId), nowMs - t.entryMs);
    }
}

The same core in Kotlin (translated by hand, not compiled in this session):

enum class VehicleType { BIKE, CAR, TRUCK }

class Spot(val id: Int, val type: VehicleType) {
    val taken = java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean(false)
    fun fits(v: VehicleType) = v.ordinal <= type.ordinal
}
class Ticket(val id: String, val spot: Spot, val plate: String, val entryMs: Long, val kind: VehicleType)

interface PricingStrategy { fun fee(v: VehicleType, durationMs: Long): Long }
class HourlyPricing : PricingStrategy {
    private val perHour = mapOf(VehicleType.BIKE to 10L, VehicleType.CAR to 30L, VehicleType.TRUCK to 80L)
    override fun fee(v: VehicleType, durationMs: Long) =
        maxOf(1L, (durationMs + 3_599_999) / 3_600_000) * perHour.getValue(v)
}

class ParkingLot(private val spots: List<Spot>, private val pricing: PricingStrategy) {
    private val live = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap<String, Ticket>()
    private val ids = java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger()

    fun park(plate: String, v: VehicleType, now: Long): Ticket? {
        while (true) {
            val s = spots.filter { !it.taken.get() && it.fits(v) }
                .minByOrNull { it.type.ordinal } ?: return null          // tightest fit, nearest first
            if (s.taken.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
                val t = Ticket("T${ids.incrementAndGet()}", s, plate, now, v)
                live[t.id] = t
                return t
            }
        }
    }

    fun unpark(id: String, now: Long): Long {
        val t = live.remove(id) ?: error("unknown ticket $id")
        val fee = pricing.fee(t.kind, now - t.entryMs)
        t.spot.taken.set(false)
        return fee
    }
}

Notes on choices: taken is an AtomicBoolean from the start so the thread-safe version can reuse Spot. NearestFreeSpot prefers the tightest fit so a bike does not waste a truck spot. Fee uses integer ceil math (ms + 3_599_999) / 3_600_000 to avoid floating point.

Common interview traps.

  • Using double for money; use integer minor units.
  • Letting a bike take a truck spot while a bike spot is free.

notes.title: Run and test
notes.html:
public class Demo {
    static List<Spot> spots() {
        return new ArrayList<>(List.of(new Spot(1, VehicleType.BIKE), new Spot(2, VehicleType.CAR),
            new Spot(3, VehicleType.CAR), new Spot(4, VehicleType.TRUCK)));
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        ParkingLot lot = new ParkingLot(spots(), new NearestFreeSpot(), new HourlyPricing());
        Ticket t = lot.park("KA01", VehicleType.CAR, 0).get();
        System.out.println("car got spot " + t.spot.id);                       // 2
        System.out.println("bike got spot " + lot.park("KA02", VehicleType.BIKE, 0).get().spot.id); // 1
        long fee = lot.unpark(t.id, 2 * 3_600_000L + 60_000);                  // 2h01m -> 3 billable hours
        System.out.println("fee = " + fee);                                    // 90
        lot.park("KA03", VehicleType.CAR, 0); lot.park("KA04", VehicleType.CAR, 0);
        System.out.println("truck fits? " + lot.park("KA05", VehicleType.TRUCK, 0).isPresent()); // true: the TRUCK spot (4) is still free

        // concurrency: 5 spots, 40 threads, exactly 5 may win
        List<Spot> five = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) five.add(new Spot(i, VehicleType.CAR));
        ParkingLot safe = new SafeParkingLot(five, new NearestFreeSpot(), new HourlyPricing());
        ExecutorService ex = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(16);
        AtomicInteger wins = new AtomicInteger();
        CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);
        List<Future<?>> fs = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 40; i++) { final int n = i;
            fs.add(ex.submit(() -> { go.await(); if (safe.park("P" + n, VehicleType.CAR, 0).isPresent()) wins.incrementAndGet(); return null; })); }
        go.countDown();
        for (Future<?> f : fs) f.get();
        ex.shutdown();
        System.out.println("safe wins = " + wins.get());                       // 5
    }
}

Actual output from javac Demo.java && java Demo:

car got spot 2
bike got spot 1
fee = 90
truck fits? true
safe wins = 5

The last line is the concurrency check: 40 threads fight for 5 spots and exactly 5 win.

Common interview traps.

  • Saying "I would test it" without naming cases: full lot, exact hour boundary, unknown ticket, double exit.
  • Tests that depend on the real clock; pass time in as a parameter, as here.

notes.title: Concurrency
notes.html:
The race. ParkingLot.park does check-then-act: pick a free spot, then mark it taken. Two gates running at once can both pick spot 2, so two cars get one spot. HashMap and ++seq are also unsafe.

Fix options, with gravity.

  1. One big synchronized on park and unpark. Simple and correct; throughput limited to one entry at a time, which is fine for one lot (a gate handles maybe 1 car every 5 s). Reversible.
  2. Compare-and-set on the spot (below). Lock-free claim; many gates proceed in parallel.
  3. A database row lock or unique constraint (UPDATE spots SET taken=1 WHERE id=? AND taken=0, check rows updated). Needed when many servers run the lot service.

The thread-safe version uses option 2: the strategy only suggests a spot, then compareAndSet(false, true) decides who really gets it, and the loser retries with the next best.

class SafeParkingLot extends ParkingLot {
    private final AtomicInteger ids = new AtomicInteger();
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, Ticket> live = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final ConcurrentHashMap<String, VehicleType> kinds = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    SafeParkingLot(List<Spot> spots, SpotStrategy s, PricingStrategy p) { super(spots, s, p); }

    @Override Optional<Ticket> park(String plate, VehicleType v, long nowMs) {
        while (true) {                                          // retry if another thread grabs our pick
            Optional<Spot> pick = strategy.pick(spots, v);
            if (pick.isEmpty()) return Optional.empty();
            Spot s = pick.get();
            if (s.taken.compareAndSet(false, true)) {           // atomic claim: only one thread wins
                Ticket t = new Ticket("T" + ids.incrementAndGet(), s, plate, nowMs);
                live.put(t.id, t); kinds.put(t.id, v);
                return Optional.of(t);
            }
        }
    }

    @Override long unpark(String ticketId, long nowMs) {
        Ticket t = live.remove(ticketId);                       // remove is atomic: double exit fails
        if (t == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("unknown ticket " + ticketId);
        long fee = pricing.fee(kinds.remove(ticketId), nowMs - t.entryMs);
        t.spot.taken.set(false);                                // free the spot last
        return fee;
    }
}

Production detail. Free the spot after computing the fee and removing the ticket, and remove from the map atomically, so a double scan of one ticket at the exit cannot charge or free twice. Symptom of the bug in production: two cars with the same spot on the display board, found by comparing active ticket count to taken-spot count.

Everyday analogy. Two people reaching for the last seat: only the one whose hand lands first (the CAS) sits; the other looks for another seat.

Common interview traps.

  • Marking park as synchronized but leaving unpark unsynchronized.
  • Using volatile boolean for the flag: visibility without atomicity does not stop double booking.
  • Locking in the strategy instead of at the claim point.

notes.title: Follow-ups
notes.html:
• Multiple floors. Add Floor holding spots; the lot asks each floor in order, or the strategy picks floor by availability. Mostly an extension of SpotStrategy.
  • Display board "free spots per type". Keep a counter per type updated on park/unpark (LongAdder) instead of scanning.
  • Lost ticket / daily cap. New PricingStrategy implementations; no change to the lot.
  • Many entrances on many servers. State moves to a database; use the row-level claim from Concurrency option 3.
  • Reservations. Add a RESERVED state to the spot with an expiry.
  • Find my car. Index plate to ticket with a second map.

Common interview traps.

  • Re-designing everything for each follow-up instead of naming which single class changes.
  • Not saying what you would give up (simplicity) when adding scale.

notes.title: Summary
notes.html:
• Entities: Spot, Ticket, ParkingLot, enum VehicleType; strategies for spot choice and price.
  • Strategy pattern isolates what changes (rules, price); Facade keeps the API to two methods; avoid Singleton.
  • Ticket holds its spot so exit is O(1); fee uses integer ceil hours.
  • Race: check-then-act on a spot. Fix with CAS on the spot (or a DB conditional update across servers); remove tickets atomically.
  • Follow-ups map to one class each: floors, display counters, new pricing, reservations.
